candidates.title: Erdős 3: finite diagonal-pullback nonoptimality
candidates.statement: At modulus 13, the supplied 79-point subset B of (Z/13Z)^2 avoids (x,y), (x,y+d), (x,y+2d), (x+d,y) for every nonzero d. The maximum size of a cyclic four-AP-free subset A of Z/13Z is exactly 6, attained by {0,1,2,4,5,7}. Hence |B|=79>78>=13|A| for every such A. In particular, every diagonal pullback S_A={(x,y):x-y belongs to A} has size 13|A|<=78 and is beaten by B. The source-faithful bridge kernel-checks the original pullback cardinality identity |S_A|=13|A|, the L-free transfer and its strict comparison with B.
candidates.proof_status: The cyclic sharpness certificate and source-faithful diagonal-pullback bridge passed Lean 4.33.1 / Mathlib 0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474 with standard axioms only. The bridge passed a fresh seven-module source-only replay on 3 October 2026, with no reused project-local compiled objects. It checks the actual pullback cardinality, its L-free transfer and the strict comparison with the retained 79-point witness. No native_decide or admitted theorem occurs in the successful chain.
candidates.prior_work_and_novelty_assessment: The 79-point witness, the separation 79>78 and its completed formal certificate are team work, as confirmed by the user. Peluse's L-configuration work provides relevant external context; the bounded review located no exact primary prior for this finite separation and does not establish world priority. Its relevance as a recognized obstacle for the parent conjecture remains a review question.
candidates.attribution: Retained SakanaAI/autolab-100 packet on branch hamdi-abderrahmene; archive-declared commit a59f286ca8965a46cb8c70deb9d01847bdaa70bb. The source ledger uses the internal label external; the user confirms team ownership of this work. The split proof, cyclic upper certificate, combination theorem and six-point sharpness certificate are explicitly dated reconstructions in this review.
candidates.route: One provisional finite-obstruction M1 review candidate combining the team witness, separation and complete certificate. Novelty and relevance require claim-specific review. M2 may be an alternative for a genuine useful formalization delta; no duplicate family or modality credit.
candidates.limits: No strong-L optimum, asymptotic improvement or solution/refutation of Erdős–Turán. The original Fugu3_Lshape one-way transfer remains valid and unchanged.
candidates.proof_outline: The retained 79-point table is checked row by row. A finite Boolean case tree excludes cyclic four-AP-free sets of size seven; a proved bridge transfers that Boolean exclusion to Finset cardinality. A kernel-checked six-point witness supplies the matching lower endpoint. The combination theorem uses 13·6=78<79. The generator is outside the proof trust boundary because the generated propositions and proofs are checked by Lean. The retained original image bijection proves card(S_A)=13*card(A), and explicit predicate equivalences connect it to the cyclic and strong-L certificates. A checked endpoint combines all of these statements for the actual source-defined pullback.
candidates.our_contribution: Our team supplies the 79-point strong-L-free witness at modulus 13, the finite separation 79>78, and the complete formal certificate that every source-defined diagonal pullback of a cyclic four-progression-free subset of Z/13Z has size at most 78 and is strictly smaller than the retained witness. The certificate also proves the sharp cyclic four-progression-free maximum of six, linking the witness and obstruction in one contribution.

candidates.title: Grothendieck: restricted sign-matrix bounds
candidates.statement: For every n and every 3-by-n sign matrix A, Q_V(A)<=sqrt(3/2) C(A) in every real inner-product space V. Additionally Q_V(A)<=sqrt(2) C(A) for the four literal archived matrices A_6x6_106, A_6x8_690, A_7x8_53110 and A_s8x8_1705. Q_V is the unit-vector objective supremum, with Q_V(A)=0 for an empty feasible set, and C is its real scalar specialization. These supporting cases form one review family.
candidates.proof_status: Fresh Row3Granular and four-case SemanticTestGranular checks passed in Lean 4.33.1 with standard axioms only. The September 25 internal record is team history, not independent prior publication; exact priority still requires comparison.

candidates.route: One provisional restricted-bound focus candidate; assess M1 after novelty and exact-target review, or M2 for a genuinely new reusable formalization. No per-case or duplicate modality credit.
candidates.limits: Fresh checking covers Row3 and four named semantic matrices only. No fresh replay of all 555 semantic cases, no global orbit-coverage theorem, no unrestricted real Grothendieck constant result and no bit-minimality claim.
candidates.proof_outline: Row3 normalizes each sign column to one of four projective types. Walsh multiplicities give four lower anchors for C; Parseval and Cauchy–Schwarz bound the vector objective by sqrt(3/2)C. Each of the four explicit semantic cases combines literal rational sum-of-squares dual data, a scalar sign witness and a generic finite-span bridge valid for arbitrary real inner-product spaces. Matrix dimensions are distinct from ambient vector dimension.

candidates.title: Matrix multiplication: one-leg rigidity
candidates.statement: For each of the three stored 139-support HKS seeds, every 81-by-23 rational matrix formed from columnwise products of two 23-by-9 factor lists has column rank 23. Thus fixing any two factor lists uniquely determines the third through the coefficient equations; changing only that list cannot reduce support while retaining the same tensor. The standard-kernel formal certificates prove all three pairings and remaining-factor uniqueness for each of the three stored seeds.
candidates.proof_status: All three stored HKS139 seeds have standard-kernel certificates for the UV, UW and VW rational injectivity and remaining-factor uniqueness statements. Seed 0 retains its recorded certificate; the two additional seeds passed fresh 71-module Lean 4.33.1 replays on 3 October 2026. Endpoint axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The original factors, selected minors, integer inverse tables and all 729 tensor coefficients match their source data. The independent exact rank checks are also retained.
candidates.prior_work_and_novelty_assessment: The rank-23/support-139 construction is explicitly attributed to Smirnov/HKS; standard linear algebra supplies the injectivity argument. The team's contribution is the specific fixed-seed one-leg obstruction and its certificates. Its prior occurrence and meaningful mathematical novelty are not established. The result is not a new matrix-multiplication algorithm or global tensor-rank bound.
candidates.attribution: Source owner Hamdi Abderrahmene; original scheme attributed in its README to Smirnov, recovered from HKS. candidates.title: Ramsey: exact weighted construction and formal lifting
candidates.statement: The literal symmetric 1024-block binary template has positive integer weights summing to Q=47,314,248 and ordered weighted monochromatic K4 probability P=75525646867723584998137743109/2505750190359427899123170347008. Exact computation gives P<20480989/679477248, the archived hill threshold. The general formal lifting theorem gives c4<=P; for t>0 and tQ>=4 the finite blow-up density differs from P by at most 6/(tQ).
candidates.proof_status: The numerator is independently checked by exact C++/Python arithmetic and matches a nonfinal validation receipt. The general count-to-limit development freshly compiled after four compatibility edits in Lean 4.33.1, with standard axioms only. It is a credible stronger prior announcement under review: a complete proof/certificate was not obtained, and the page's publication/version before the event has not been authenticated. The team's construction therefore remains a provisional M1 candidate pending that verification. Lifting, averaging and collision estimates are known mathematics. Mathlib edge/Turan density infrastructure and public lean-flag-algebras uniform blow-up and limit developments provide genuine formal overlap, while no matching complete weighted Ramsey interface was located in the bounded comparison. candidates.title: Busy Beaver 6: exact halting witness
candidates.statement: Starting on a bi-infinite blank tape in state A, the six-state two-symbol machine 1RB0LC_1RD1RB_0LH1LE_1LA1LD_0LA1LF_0LE0RD executes exactly 1,235,211 transitions to H with 1,519 ones on its final tape and no earlier halted prefix. Every state A–F is visited by step 40. Separate exact simulators give final head -2001 and visited span 2,028 (minimum -2001, maximum 26, including the post-halting head); head and span are not kernel-certified claims.
candidates.proof_status: A new standard-kernel certificate in Lean 4.33.1 successfully checks the literal machine, exact run, final ones count, absence of an earlier halt and all-six-states visitation. Claims.lean endpoints exact_halting_witness and visits_all_six_states have only propext and Quot.sound in their printed axiom sets. The 129-source-module closure uses no native_decide, custom axiom or admission, and requires no Mathlib. Semantics.lean proves the tape-cell equations for both move directions. Original dictionary- and set-tape simulator records are preserved as independent evidence.
